issue.title: Feature request: add a SkillInvocation hook event

relevant_locations.role: Existing analytics tracking method for skill invocations

llm_context.input_title: Feature request: add a SkillInvocation hook event
llm_context.input_body: No body provided in issue description.

generated_output.summary: This issue proposes adding a new 'SkillInvocation' hook event to Codex hooks (`[features] hooks = true`). Currently, tool calls, prompts, and session lifecycle events notify external hook handlers, but explicit and implicit skill activations remain invisible to external handlers.
generated_output.root_cause_analysis: Hook dispatching currently handles events like user prompt submission or tool calls, but lacks an emission site and hook runtime plumbing for `HookEventName::SkillInvocation` alongside the existing analytics and OTEL emission sites in `skills.rs`.

step_by_step_plan.title: Inspect Skill Invocation Control Flow
step_by_step_plan.description: Examine how track_skill_invocations is called within codex-rs/analytics/src/client.rs and related skill handling files to identify where skill invocation events are triggered.

step_by_step_plan.title: Define HookEventName::SkillInvocation
step_by_step_plan.description: Add the new SkillInvocation variant to the hook event enumeration in the hooks module, ensuring it includes metadata such as skill name, file path, scope, invocation type, turn ID, and session ID.

step_by_step_plan.title: Wire Skill Invocation Dispatcher
step_by_step_plan.description: Integrate the hook dispatch call alongside track_skill_invocations whenever a skill is explicitly or implicitly invoked in the skill execution runtime.

step_by_step_plan.title: Add Regression Test
step_by_step_plan.description: Implement a unit test verifying that invoking a skill successfully dispatches the SkillInvocation hook event with the expected payload to external hook handlers.

step_by_step_plan.title: Run Test Suite
step_by_step_plan.description: Execute cargo test to verify that the new SkillInvocation hook event passes all test assertions without breaking existing telemetry or hook mechanisms.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: The mechanism by which internal system events are serialized and dispatched to external hook handlers.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Understanding how events flow from core subsystems to external handlers allows developers to expose new telemetry and audit points safely.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Fixing this issue requires adding a new `SkillInvocation` hook event that mirrors existing hook dispatch patterns.

structured_concepts.short_explanation: Internal analytics tracking records usage metrics, whereas external hooks notify user-configured external scripts and handlers.
structured_concepts.why_it_matters: Separating internal analytics from user hooks ensures telemetry stays private while giving users audit capability.
structured_concepts.connection_to_issue: Skill invocations are already tracked via analytics; this feature extends them to the hook runtime so external handlers receive them too.

common_pitfalls: Forgetting to wire the new hook event through `core/src/hook_runtime.rs` so handlers can actually receive it.
Attempting to make `SkillInvocation` a blocking hook event instead of a notification event.
Incomplete serialization of fields such as `skill_path`, `scope`, or `invocation_type`.
